title: Repeated query cache behavior
question: The same search question is asked repeatedly. Explain the literal in-memory cache lookup and return behavior shown here and propose how to check for unnecessary requests.

findings.statement: When a query string's SHA‑256 identity is already present in the in‑memory _query_cache, embed_query moves the entry to the end of the OrderedDict to mark it as most‑recently used and returns a copy of the cached NumPy array.

If the query identity is not cached, embed_query performs a remote request via _request, stores a copy of the returned vector in _query_cache, moves it to the end, and evicts the least‑recently used entry when the cache exceeds QUERY_CACHE_SIZE.

missing_information: Exact value of QUERY_CACHE_SIZE and whether it is configurable at runtime.
Implementation details of the _request method to confirm it performs network I/O.
next_steps: Add instrumentation (e.g., logging or metrics counters) around the cache‑hit check and the _request call to record how often the cache is used versus a remote request is made.
Write a test that calls embed_query repeatedly with the same question and asserts that the underlying _request method is invoked only once, confirming that subsequent calls hit the in‑memory cache.
